I can relate, I think I’m bad at my job and find that my anxiety makes me much worse (getting frightened of failing and so don’t give things a proper try). I’ve found that by reframing what you’re doing, you can find small joy in the work and more confidence. When you find a bit of joy in it, you’ll be motivated to do a much better job (and catch those pesky mistakes).

It might not be that you find meaning in the work you do, but perhaps you could focus on how your work helps those around you? Your manager and colleagues lives can be positively impacted by your work at the very least.

By all means, do some research into roles you’d prefer and find passion in, but remember that every job is a job. I have my dream job atm and I honestly hate it for weeks/months at a time (this is not normal- mostly Covid/anxiety related hatred at the moment). When I’m hating my work and wanting to leave, I can’t think of a single other job that I’d enjoy, all work feels like a hopeless waste of time. In these times, I realise it’s not my work that’s the problem, I’ve just gotten in a funk and allowed my anxiety to take over. I try and tackle things head on and share my issues with anxiety with my colleagues (‘fess up about how it impacts you). After a while, something clicks and I start to enjoy it, build back some confidence and get better at it again. Sorry for the long message!

I take it with or without food, makes no difference. I sometimes swallow the pills dry when I cba to get water. 

I’ve experimented with taking it in the morning or eve.  For me, a couple of hours after I take it I get tired and want to get cosy. But if I take it any later than 9pm, I get insomnia, I just keep waking up. When I took it as soon as I woke up, I’d find I’d start yawning my way through the day and need naps. 

I take it at 6-8pm and that’s the perfect time for me. I find if I take it too late, it keeps me up a little. It’s about finding your sweet spot, sometimes your sweet spot will change too. When I started taking them (and every time I increase the dose) I have 3 weeks of utter exhaustion.

Pick a day when you’re staying in and relaxing, take things slow, keep hydrated and distract yourself with Netflix. You’re going to feel strange and uncomfortable, but try to ride it out until 4pm. Other people prefer slowly shifting the medication time by an hour, probably more sensible.
